To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mice overexpressing Sim2 show mild learning and memory defects.
mSim2 is expressed in the hippocampus and amydgala of adult mice and that mice overexpressing this gene exhibit mild defects in learning and memory.

Mice overexpressing the Sim2 gene, located on human chromosome-21 and Drosophila chromosome 3, show a moderate impairment of learning and a mild impairment of memory, which may serve as a model of mental retardation in Down's syndrome.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of the most common human chromosomal anomaly, the trisomy 21 or Down's syndrome (see also the project of Dr. M. Kozlovsky).
the molecular mechanisms underlying mental retardation in trisomy 21, the genetic disorder known as Down's syndrome ( DS ).
the role of mSim2 in the pathogenesis of mental retardation in Down's syndrome and the role of the beta-2 adrenergic receptor in the pathogenesis and treatment of Alzheimer's disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Sim2 is a critical gene for normal learning and memory in mammals, and that overdosage or underdosage of the protein is associated with learning and memory defects in mice and humans, respectively.
mSim2 overexpressing transgenic mouse is a good model for studying the pathogenesis and treatment of Down's syndrome.
the present study has shown that mice overexpressing Sim2 have some learning and memory impairment, and that this may be a useful animal model for the mental retardation in Down's syndrome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mSim2 is a candidate for the gene responsible for the mental retardation in Down's syndrome.

the Sim2 gene may play a critical role in the development of the central and peripheral nervous system in mice, and that the Sim2 overexpressing mice may be a good model to study the role of the human chromosome 21 in Down's syndrome.
Sim2 overexpression in mice causes a mild impairment of learning and/or memory, and this is a new animal model for the study of Down's syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Sim2 gene is a critical player for learning and memory in mammals.

Sim2 is expressed in adult brain, that mice overexpressing Sim2 exhibit a moderate defect of fear conditioning and a milder defect of the spatial memory test, that the defect in fear conditioning is more pronounced than the defect in spatial memory test, and that the defects are likely to be due to overdosage of the gene product.
Sim2 is expressed in the brain and is critical for learning and memory.
